title: Morning light
science_note: Morning light sets your body clock and raises cortisol at the right time.

tiny.text: Step outside and face the sky. No sunglasses.

standard.text: Go outside in your first hour awake. Look toward the sky, not at the sun. No sunglasses.

stretch.text: Stay outside 30 min. Cloudy days need the longer time.

todo: Book file says 5–10 min on clear days, 15 min partly cloudy, 30 min overcast. engine-spec says 10–30 min. App uses engine-spec. Confirm.
Tiny '1 min' comes from the Figma Busy day sheet, not from the book.

title: Same sleep times
science_note: A steady sleep and wake time improves sleep quality.

tiny.text: Set tomorrow's wake alarm to your usual time.

standard.text: Go to bed and wake up at the same time, within 30 min.

stretch.text: Keep the same times on weekends too.

todo: SL04b (1-week chronotype test) is a task, not included here.

title: Caffeine cutoff
science_note: Caffeine blocks the sleep signal (adenosine) and stays in your body for hours.

tiny.text: Pick a decaf drink for your afternoon cup.

standard.text: No caffeine in the 10 hours before bed. Best: none after 14:00.

stretch.text: No caffeine in the 12 hours before bed. Stay under 400 mg a day.

title: Delay coffee
science_note: Waiting a bit for coffee can help prevent the afternoon energy crash.

tiny.text: Drink a glass of water first. Coffee can wait.

standard.text: Have your first coffee 60 min after waking.

stretch.text: Have your first coffee 90 min after waking.

todo: Needs are [fog, energy], from the symptom map in engine-spec section 1 (SL11b is listed under Foggy and Always tired).
Skip this patch on mornings with a hard workout right after waking (book note).

title: Daily steps
science_note: Daily walking is the base for heart and brain health.

tiny.text: Stand up and walk to the nearest window.

title: Walk after meals
science_note: A short walk after eating keeps blood sugar lower and cuts the sleepy dip.

tiny.text: Stand up and take a few steps after you eat.

standard.text: Walk 5–10 min within 30 min after a meal.

title: Air squats
science_note: Squats wake up your leg muscles and get blood moving again.

tiny.text: Stand up from your chair once, slowly.

stretch.text: 10 air squats every 45 min of sitting.

todo: duration_min = 1 is an estimate for 10 squats. Not in engine-spec. Confirm.

title: Sitting break
science_note: Long sitting switches off muscles and slows your metabolism.

tiny.text: Soleus pushups: while seated, lift and lower your heels.

standard.text: Move for 5 min after 30 min of sitting.

stretch.text: Move 5 min for every 30 min of sitting, all work day.

title: Water on waking
science_note: Your body is low on water after sleep.

standard.text: Drink 500 ml of water after waking, before coffee or breakfast.

stretch.text: Drink 700 ml of water after waking, before coffee or breakfast.

todo: duration_min = 1 is an estimate. Not in engine-spec. Confirm.

title: Daily water

tiny.text: Fill a water bottle and put it on your desk.

standard.text: Drink 2.4 L of water in your first 10 hours awake.

stretch.text: 2.4 L in 10 hours, spread out: a glass every hour.

title: Protein at meals
science_note: Protein keeps you full and protects muscle.

tiny.text: Add one protein food, like a yogurt.

standard.text: Eat 30–50 g of protein at this meal.

stretch.text: 30–50 g of protein at every full meal today.

todo: duration_min = 5 comes from Figma (Pick patches: 'Protein breakfast · 5 min'), not engine-spec.

title: Physiological sigh
science_note: A double inhale and a long exhale slows your heart rate fast.

tiny.text: One sigh: two inhales through the nose, then one long exhale through the mouth.

standard.text: 1–3 physiological sighs: inhale deep through the nose, add a short second inhale, then exhale slowly through the mouth.

stretch.text: 5 min of slow sighs, breathing in this pattern.

title: Morning meditation
science_note: Focusing on your breath calms the body step by step.

tiny.text: In bed, close your eyes and take one slow breath through your nose.

standard.text: Right after waking, sit still for 5 min, eyes closed. Breathe slowly through your nose.

stretch.text: 5 min, and stay put even if you feel the urge to grab your phone.

title: Micro-rests
science_note: Short pauses help your brain lock in what you just learned.

tiny.text: Pause 10 s with your eyes closed. No phone.

standard.text: Between work blocks, pause 5–30 s. Close your eyes or look at nothing.

stretch.text: Take a 5–10 min break with no new input: no phone, no talking.
